summary: Treasury cash-management domain foundation adds bank-account approval, cash-position snapshots, liquidity forecast projections, cash-transfer proposal metadata, and SAP FI/TRM parity-map linkage while explicitly refusing durable persistence, bank-network calls, payment execution, accounting ledger mutation, Workflow execution, cloud deployment, and runtime audit-chain claims.

findings: The implementation is a small pure-domain validation/calculation model, not a treasury workstation or ERP monolith clone.
Cash position, forecast, and transfer proposal calculations are deterministic guard-clause logic with no hidden side effects.
Flat treasury microservice destination improves SAP FI/TRM parity without creating microservices/erp.
Capability flags and evidence rows keep cloud/runtime claims honest until adapters and bank rails land.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if unapproved bank accounts, missing cash positions, currency mismatches, insufficient source surplus, invalid dates, unsafe refs, credential-shaped evidence refs, lowercase currency values, or no-need transfers are accepted.
findings: Positive treasury cash flow and negative guard rails are covered.
Types map directly to bank account approval, cash position, liquidity forecast, and cash-transfer proposal concepts common to treasury cash-management systems.
Focused treasury tests/clippy, ERP parity map tests/clippy, enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan are recorded in verification.

alternatives_named: add treasury cash domain foundation first
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: A flat domain foundation gives ERP FI/TRM parity a service-owned first write path while keeping bank networks, payments, storage, Workflow, and cloud adapters out of scope.
rejected_reasons: Accounting-only composition left SAP TRM cash management without a bounded service owner.
Payment/bank-network runtime requires external rails, authorization, secrets, and durable audit storage beyond this slice.

findings: No credentials, external network calls, payment rails, or bank connectivity are introduced.
Source and audit refs reject traversal, whitespace/control, and credential-shaped strings.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Pure string/date/money validation and arithmetic only; no I/O or unbounded data access exists.

findings.summary: No database, network, filesystem, or hot runtime path is introduced.

data_class_touched: FINANCIAL balances, inflows, outflows, transfer amounts, and shortfall metadata
findings: SAP/Oracle official materials inform cash-management coverage only; no exhaustive vendor parity or proprietary behavior clone is claimed.
The change is additive: one new crate/spec/catalog row and parity-map references; no migration or external resource is introduced.
Static evidence, task rows, and audit-chain rows document the change; runtime audit emission remains a non-claim.
No production user or data migration exists.
Package name follows oya-treasury-cash-domain and flat microservice layout.
Machine-readable treasury spec and existing task ledger capture the slice without creating root markdown sprawl.
New code is isolated to microservices/treasury plus Enterprise Suite parity map references.
Clean architecture is preserved: domain crate depends only on data boundary kernel and std.
No new third-party dependencies were added; Cargo.lock changed only for the new workspace package.
specs/microservices/treasury.json parses successfully and evidence follows prior multispectrum shape.
Cash position, liquidity forecast, and transfer proposal arithmetic is deterministic exact currency-matched validation with no tolerance or hidden state.

M1_challenge_assumption.finding: Challenged whether treasury should be folded into accounting; creating a separate cash-management domain is more aligned with ERP FI/TRM parity and future cloud integration.

M2_zoomed_out_fit.finding: Complements HR/payroll/accounting/procurement foundations and improves ERP parity while keeping no microservices/erp monolith.
